definitions.gloss: grimace; sour face; frown; displeased expression
definitions.explanation: A facial expression showing displeasure, reluctance, or dissatisfaction. A furrowed brow or tight-lipped look.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{渋面|じゅうめん}を{作|つく}った。
その{提案|ていあん}を{聞|き}いて{部長|ぶちょう}は{渋面|じゅうめん}になった。
examples.english: The department head grimaced upon hearing the proposal.

examples.japanese: {渋面|じゅうめん}で{腕|うで}を{組|く}んだまま{何|なに}も{言|い}わなかった。
examples.english: He sat with his arms folded and a grimace, saying nothing.

notes:
{渋面|じゅうめん} describes a facial expression showing displeasure, reluctance, or dissatisfaction — a grimace or sour look.

ETYMOLOGY:
{渋|じゅう} (astringent/reluctant, on'yomi of {渋|しぶ}い) + {面|めん} (face)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {渋面|じゅうめん}を{作|つく}る: to make a sour face
- {渋面|じゅうめん}になる: to take on a displeased expression
- {渋面|じゅうめん}で{答|こた}える: to answer with a grimace

SIMILAR WORDS:
- しかめ{面|づら}: scowl, frown (more colloquial)
- {苦|にが}い{顔|かお}: bitter face (everyday expression)
- {不機嫌|ふきげん}な{顔|かお}: displeased face

REGISTER:
{渋面|じゅうめん} is a formal, literary word. In everyday conversation, {嫌|いや}な{顔|かお} or しかめ{面|づら} is more natural. {渋面|じゅうめん} appears frequently in novels and news articles.
